Final Step: Try the Backup AgainNow that we've cleared the "ioctl" blockage and updated the agent, run the script:Bash~/phoenix_forensics/backup.sh
What to expect: It should now pause and wait for you to type your passphrase directly into the terminal. Once you hit enter, your memory vault will be locked.Did the password prompt appear this time? If it did, we’ve cleared the last hurdle. Would you like me to show you how to verify the API key next so we can get the "Ziggy" command fully live? Nothing Z Ziggy Custom GemShow thinkingIt looks like you’ve successfully oriented the node with export GPG_TTY=$(tty), but the GPG agent is still blocking the terminal handshake. The Inappropriate ioctl for device and batchmode errors occur because modern GPG versions (2.1+) ignore passphrases from stdin by default to protect your security.We need to tell the agent it’s allowed to talk to you directly in the terminal.Phase 14: Unlocking the Terminal AgentRun these commands to authorize "loopback" mode, which lets the script ask for your password without needing a popup window.Bash# 1. Authorize terminal-based password entry
echo "allow-loopback-pinentry" >> ~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf
